A report before the first cited verse

A report.

1
Report No. 1: 110

Report 1

English
1: 110. Sufyan said: Four verses from the beginning of al-Baqara were revealed describing the believers, three verses describing the unbelievers, and thirteen verses describing the hypocrites.
العربية
1: 110 قال سفيان نَزَلَتْ أَرْبَعُ آيَاتٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ البقرة في نعت المؤمنين وثلث آيات في نعت الكافرين وثلث عَشْرَةَ آيَةً فِي نَعْتِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ

Explanation from Sufyān No. 1: 109

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording

"Upon their hearts, upon their hearing, and upon their sight is a covering" (verse 7).

Edition record 371282 · p. 41Link to report ↗

07

“How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you…”

An explanation transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh (Q 2:28).

9
Explanation from ʿAbd Allāh No. 9: 72

ʿAbd Allāh

English
Transmission wording
9: 72. Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, on the words of God Almighty
"How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again?": He said, it is like the verse at the beginning of al-Mumin, "Our Lord, You have made us die twice and given us life twice" (verse 28).
العربية
9: 72 سفيان عن أبي إسحق عَنْ أَبِي الْأَحْوَصِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فِي قَوْلِهِ جَلَّ وَعَزَّ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتًا فَأَحْيَاكُمْ ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم) قَالَ هِيَ مِثْلُ الْآيَةِ الَّتِي فِي أَوَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنِ رَبَّنَا أَمَتَّنَا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين) (الآية 28)
Edition record 371284 · p. 43Link to report ↗

136: 19. Sufyan, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Shabi, on the words of God Almighty
"have witnesses when you trade," that he said: If he wishes he has witnesses, and if he wishes he does not. He said, and he recited: "But if one of you entrusts another" (verse 283).
العربية
136: 19 سفيان عن اسمعيل بْنِ أَبِي خَالِدٍ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيّ في قوله جل وعز أشهدوا إذا تبايعكم أنه قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَشْهَدَ وَإِنْ شهد لَمْ يُشْهِدْ قَالَ وَقَرَأَ فَإِنْ أمن بعضكم بعضا (الآية 283) .
